info.name: Smart Refrigerator IoT Backend
info.description:
# Smart Refrigerator IoT Backend - end-to-end test collection

## What you need
1. Backend running: `docker compose up -d postgres emqx` then `mvn spring-boot:run` (or `docker compose up --build`).
2. EMQX reachable on http://localhost:18083 (dashboard/API) with admin / public.
3. (Optional) an MQTT subscriber to watch backend-to-device traffic: `mosquitto_sub -h localhost -p 1883 -t 'appliance/#' -v`.
4. Two small files for firmware upload tests: `printf 'hello' > fw.bin`.

## How MQTT is simulated
Postman collections cannot publish MQTT, so every "Publish ..." request calls EMQX's HTTP API (`POST /api/v5/publish`) with the exact topic and JSON payload a refrigerator MCU would send.
The following GET request (1.5 s delay) checks what the backend stored.

## Run order
Run folders 0 -> 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 5 sequentially (Collection Runner or one by one). Folder 5B needs lowered thresholds, folder 6 needs file selection for the upload requests, folder 7 is manual, folder 8 cleans up.
Variables (`deviceId`, `deviceIdB`, `firmwareId`, `jobId`, ...) are filled automatically by test scripts.

## Timing rules to remember
* A device is ONLINE only if it sent telemetry in the last 90 s - rerun a Publish telemetry step if you pause for long.
* Spike filter: a jump larger than 15 C within 30 s of the previous reading is dropped (steps 2.6-2.9).
* Alert rules use server receive time: defaults are 15 min (fridge/freezer), 5 min (door), 6 h (compressor).

item.name: 0. Setup and health checks
item.description: Run these first. Confirms the backend is up, the OpenAPI document is served, and obtains an EMQX API token used by every 'Publish ...' request (Postman cannot publish MQTT in a collection, so the EMQX HTTP API plays the role of the refrigerator MCU).

request.description:
Calls Spring Boot Actuator. If this fails, start the stack (`docker compose up -d postgres emqx` then `mvn spring-boot:run`) and check the datasource settings.

**Expected result:** 200 with {"status":"UP"}.

Confirms springdoc is serving the generated spec. Swagger UI is at {{baseUrl}}/swagger-ui.html.

**Expected result:** 200; paths include /api/v1/devices and /api/v1/firmware.

Logs in to the EMQX dashboard API (default admin / public) and stores the bearer token in the collection variable `emqxToken`. If EMQX forced a password change, update `emqxPass` in the environment.

**Expected result:** 200 with a token; saved to {{emqxToken}}.

item.name: 1. Device management (CRUD)
item.description: Registers two devices and exercises validation, lookup, listing, update and status. Device A (hardware rev A2) is used by all later folders; device B stays offline and is used for negative tests. MAC addresses are randomised so the folder can be re-run.

request.description:
Sends the MAC in lower case on purpose to prove it is normalised. Saves the new id as {{deviceId}}.

**Expected result:** 201; MAC upper-cased; status OFFLINE; state NORMAL_COOLING.

exec: const mac = ['AA', 'BB', hex(), hex(), hex(), hex()].join(':');

request.description:
Registers the same MAC again.

**Expected result:** 409 Conflict with an 'already registered' message.

Bean-validation check of the MAC pattern.

**Expected result:** 400 with details naming macAddress.

Empty body: macAddress, name, hardwareRev and firmwareVersion are mandatory.

**Expected result:** 400 with at least 4 field errors.

Fetch device A by UUID.

**Expected result:** 200 with the device.

Looks the device up by MAC (lower-case input is normalised).

**Expected result:** 200 with device A.

Paginated listing, newest first.

**Expected result:** 200; content includes device A.

Status filter. Device A has not sent telemetry yet so it must appear here.

**Expected result:** 200; every item OFFLINE.

exec: pm.test("all returned devices are OFFLINE", () => j.content.forEach(d => pm.expect(d.status).to.eql("OFFLINE")));

request.description:
Partial update: only supplied non-blank fields change.

**Expected result:** 200 with new name/model; hardwareRev still A2.

exec: pm.test("name and model updated", () => { pm.expect(j.name).to.eql("Kitchen Fridge (Updated)"); pm.expect(j.model).to.eql("FX-200 Pro"); });

request.description:
Lightweight status endpoint.

**Expected result:** online=false, status OFFLINE, 0 active faults.

exec: pm.test("offline, no faults", () => { pm.expect(j.online).to.eql(false); pm.expect(j.status).to.eql("OFFLINE"); pm.expect(j.activeFaultCount).to.eql(0); });

request.description:
Unknown UUID.

**Expected result:** 404 with a structured error body.

exec: pm.test("message says not found", () => pm.expect(j.message).to.include("not found"));

request.description:
A second device that never sends telemetry; used for 'offline' negative tests.

**Expected result:** 201; id saved as {{deviceIdB}}.

item.name: 2. Telemetry ingestion over MQTT
item.description: The 'Publish' requests call EMQX's HTTP publish API, which delivers exactly what an MCU would publish to `appliance/{deviceId}/telemetry`. Each publish is followed by a GET (with a 1.5 s pre-request delay) that verifies what the backend persisted. Run steps 2.6 -> 2.9 within 30 seconds of each other (spike filter window). Optional: watch traffic with `mosquitto_sub -h localhost -p 1883 -t 'appliance/#' -v`.

request.description:
Publishes {"freezerTemp":-18.5,"fridgeTemp":4.0,"compressorOn":true,"doorOpen":false}.

**Expected result:** EMQX returns 200/202; the backend receives the message on the device topic.

Reads the newest reading. If this is 404, the MQTT message did not reach the backend: check the broker URL and the backend logs.

**Expected result:** 200; reading equals the published values and is recent.

exec: // give the backend a moment to consume the MQTT message

pm.test("values match the published payload", () => { pm.expect(j.fridgeTemp).to.eql(4); pm.expect(j.freezerTemp).to.eql(-18.5); pm.expect(j.compressorOn).to.eql(true); pm.expect(j.doorOpen).to.eql(false); });
pm.test("timestamp is recent (< 60 s)", () => pm.expect(Date.now() - new Date(j.time).getTime()).to.be.below(60000));

request.description:
Every telemetry message doubles as a heartbeat and flips OFFLINE -> ONLINE.

**Expected result:** status ONLINE with lastSeenAt.

Value outside [-60, 60] C: must be filtered as noise.

**Expected result:** EMQX returns 200/202; the backend receives the message on the device topic.

The newest stored reading must still be the one from step 2.2.

**Expected result:** Same reading id as step 2.2.

exec: // give the backend a moment to consume the MQTT message

Saves its id for the spike check.

exec: // give the backend a moment to consume the MQTT message

request.description:
A 35.8 C jump within 30 s (limit 15 C) must be rejected. Run this within 30 s of step 2.6.

**Expected result:** EMQX returns 200/202; the backend receives the message on the device topic.

If you ran step 2.8 more than 30 s after 2.6, the window has passed and the reading would be accepted; just rerun 2.6-2.9.

**Expected result:** Still the 4.2 reading.

exec: // give the backend a moment to consume the MQTT message

request.description:
Third reading; gives the stats endpoint a compressor-off sample.

**Expected result:** EMQX returns 200/202; the backend receives the message on the device topic.

The backend must log and ignore it without crashing the MQTT subscriber.

**Expected result:** EMQX 200/202; backend logs an error but keeps running.

Proves 2.10 was stored and 2.11 was ignored.

**Expected result:** fridgeTemp 4.5, compressorOn false.

item.name: 4. Remote commands
item.description: Commands are published by the backend to `appliance/{deviceId}/commands` with QoS 1. To see the actual MQTT messages run `mosquitto_sub -h localhost -p 1883 -t 'appliance/+/commands' -v` (or use the EMQX dashboard WebSocket client) while running this folder. Device A must be ONLINE (folder 2 ran less than 90 s ago; if not, rerun step 2.6).

request.description:
Dispatches a defrost command and optimistically moves the state machine to DEFROST_CYCLE.

**Expected result:** 202; topic appliance/{id}/commands; protocol MQTT-QOS1.

exec: pm.test("response describes the dispatch", () => { pm.expect(j.type).to.eql("FORCE_DEFROST"); pm.expect(j.topic).to.eql("appliance/" + pm.collectionVariables.get("deviceId") + "/commands"); pm.expect(j.protocol).to.eql("MQTT-QOS1"); pm.expect(j.commandId).to.be.a("string"); });

request.description:
State pattern: DEFROST_STARTED event applied.

**Expected result:** operationalState DEFROST_CYCLE.

The MCU is the source of truth and reports the end of the defrost on `appliance/{id}/state`.

**Expected result:** EMQX returns 200/202; the backend receives the message on the device topic.

Backend adopted the device-reported state.

**Expected result:** operationalState NORMAL_COOLING.

exec: // give the backend a moment to consume the MQTT message

Fridge target 0..10 C, freezer target -30..-10 C.

**Expected result:** 202.

Business-rule validation in the service layer.

**Expected result:** 400.

Bean validation: fridge target max is 10 C.

**Expected result:** 400 with a fridgeTargetTemp error.

Enum value not supported.

**Expected result:** 400.

type is mandatory.

**Expected result:** 400.

**Expected result:** 202.

item.name: 5. Faults and device-reported alerts
item.description: Alerts published by the MCU on `appliance/{id}/alerts` become fault events. A CRITICAL fault sets the device status to FAULT and the state to CRITICAL_FAULT; a WARNING does not change the status. Device A must be ONLINE.

request.description:
Simulates a hardware fault report.

**Expected result:** EMQX returns 200/202; the backend receives the message on the device topic.

Lists active faults of device A and saves the id as {{faultId}}.

**Expected result:** One active DEVICE_REPORTED CRITICAL fault.

exec: // give the backend a moment to consume the MQTT message

pm.test("DEVICE_REPORTED / CRITICAL / mentions E21", () => { const f = j.content[0]; pm.expect(f.type).to.eql("DEVICE_REPORTED"); pm.expect(f.severity).to.eql("CRITICAL"); pm.expect(f.message).to.include("E21"); pm.expect(f.active).to.eql(true); });

request.description:
Fault engine updated the device status and state machine.

**Expected result:** status FAULT, state CRITICAL_FAULT, count 1.

exec: pm.test("FAULT with 1 active fault", () => { pm.expect(j.status).to.eql("FAULT"); pm.expect(j.activeFaultCount).to.eql(1); pm.expect(j.operationalState).to.eql("CRITICAL_FAULT"); });

request.description:
Single fault lookup.

**Expected result:** 200; active=true.

Manual resolution (an operator acknowledges the fault).

**Expected result:** 200; active=false; resolvedAt set.

Last critical fault cleared -> FAULTS_CLEARED transition.

**Expected result:** status ONLINE; state NORMAL_COOLING.

exec: pm.test("ONLINE, no faults, NORMAL_COOLING", () => { pm.expect(j.status).to.eql("ONLINE"); pm.expect(j.activeFaultCount).to.eql(0); pm.expect(j.operationalState).to.eql("NORMAL_COOLING"); });

request.description:
Resolving a resolved fault is a no-op.

**Expected result:** 200; unchanged.

Unknown id.

**Expected result:** 404.

request.description:

**Expected result:** 200.

item.name: 5B. Sustained-condition alert rules (needs lowered thresholds, ~2 min of waiting)
item.description: The built-in rules need a condition to hold for minutes (fridge > 10 C for 15 min, door open 5 min). To test them quickly start the backend with `APP_ALERTS_FRIDGE_BREACH_MINUTES=1 APP_ALERTS_DOOR_OPEN_MINUTES=1` (docker-compose: add them under backend.environment). Steps marked WAIT use a ~65 s pre-request delay. The rules use server receive time, so real waiting is required. Skip this folder with default thresholds.

request.description:
Starts the 'door open' run.

**Expected result:** EMQX returns 200/202; the backend receives the message on the device topic.

request.description:
Second 'door open' reading 65 s later -> DOOR_LEFT_OPEN fault. If your Postman limits script time, wait manually then send.

**Expected result:** operationalState DOOR_ALARM.

Door closes -> condition cleared.

**Expected result:** EMQX returns 200/202; the backend receives the message on the device topic.

Engine auto-resolves when the condition clears.

item.name: 6. Firmware management and OTA updates
item.description: Before starting: create test binaries, e.g. `printf 'hello' > fw.bin` (its SHA-256 is 2cf24dba5fb0a30e26e83b2ac5b9e29e1b161e5c1fa7425e73043362938b9824). In the three upload requests (6.2, 6.21 and the duplicate 6.3) pick the file under Body > form-data > file. In the Collection Runner enable 'Allow reading files outside working directory' or run these requests manually. Watch the OTA command with `mosquitto_sub -h localhost -p 1883 -t 'appliance/+/ota/command' -v` - it contains jobId, downloadUrl, sha256, signature and strategy DUAL_BANK.

item.name: 6.0a Heartbeat so device A is ONLINE

request.description:
Devices flip to OFFLINE after 90 s without telemetry; send a fresh reading before OTA.

**Expected result:** EMQX returns 200/202; the backend receives the message on the device topic.

OTA is rejected for OFFLINE devices.

**Expected result:** status ONLINE.

exec: // give the backend a moment to consume the MQTT message
pm.test("ONLINE or FAULT (eligible for OTA)", () => pm.expect(["ONLINE", "FAULT"]).to.include(j.status));

formdata.description: Select any small file (e.g. created with: printf 'hello' > fw.bin)

request.description:
SELECT A FILE FIRST. The pre-request script generates unique versions ({{fwVersion}} / {{fwVersion2}}). The backend streams the file to disk while computing SHA-256; compare with `sha256sum fw.bin`.

**Expected result:** 201; 64-char lowercase SHA-256; id saved as {{firmwareId}}.

exec: pm.collectionVariables.set("firmwareId", j.id); pm.collectionVariables.set("fwSha256", j.checksumSha256); pm.collectionVariables.set("fwSize", j.sizeBytes);
pm.test("download URL points at this firmware", () => pm.expect(j.downloadUrl).to.include(j.id));

**Expected result:** 202; accepted 1 / rejected 2; jobId saved.

exec: pm.test("device A accepted with a jobId", () => { pm.expect(j.results[0].accepted).to.eql(true); pm.expect(j.results[0].jobId).to.be.a("string"); });
pm.test("unknown id rejected: not found", () => pm.expect(j.results[2].reason).to.include("not found"));

request.description:

request.description:
